..
Issued at 204 AM MDT Tue Oct 27 2026

So far, the forecast is working out fairly well. An area of rain and 
snow associated with the front and trough is working its way across 
western Wyoming. It is moving quite quickly and other than a few 
orographic showers in the northwestern mountains, should be out of 
the area by sunrise, with a majority of the area dry for most of the 
day. Any snowfall amounts should remain sub advisory, but some of 
the mountain passes could be slick into the morning before the snow 
melts off after sunrise.  Our attention then turns to strong to 
potentially high wind. This will be mainly in the wind prone areas 
like around South Pass and from Muddy Gap northeastward through 
Casper.

There are some factors for it. We will have an 100 knot jet streak 
over the area today. Some models also show wind at 700 millibar 
millibars around 50 knots, especially through around 2 pm when there 
will be some decrease. There are some factors against it though. 
Most MOS guidance shows sustained winds at the Casper airport only 
around 22 to 26 knots, I would like to see 30 knots to have more 
confidence for high wind. Next, we dive into the wonderful world of 
ensemble and probabilistic guidance. The National Blend of Models 
ensemble gives a greater than 1 in 2 chance of wind gusts over 30 
mph across most of the area. However, for high wind we are 
interested in wind gusts over 55 mph. The main area with the 
strongest wind is over the higher elevations of Casper Mountain and 
the Green and Rattlesnake Ranges, where criteria is 75 mph gusts. 
There is an area on south side of Casper that has a greater than 1 
in 2 chance of gusts over 55 mph. However, criteria is higher here, 
gusts have to be over 65 mph. And chances of this are less than 1 
out of 4. There could be an isolated high wind gust in places like 
Wyoming Boulevard on the South Side of Casper and along Hat Six 
Road, but this would be the exception and not the rule. So, we chose 
not to issue a high wind warning at this time. Wind should decrease 
later this afternoon as the system moves away and the pressure 
gradient begins to relax.

A second shortwave will approach the area on Tuesday night and bring 
another round of showers. This one is similar to this one in that 1) 
It will have some upper level dynamics to work with in the form of 
the right rear quadrant of a jet streak and 2) It will be a fast 
moving system, with most of the precipitation falling in a 6 to 9 
hour period, most likely from 9 pm until around sunrise Wednesday. I 
am still concerned the current forecast may be a bit underdone on 
QPF amounts, especially in southwestern Wyoming. I could see an 
inch or two of snow in places like Kemmerer, Farson and even Big 
Piney and Pinedale with a bit more in the Salt and Wyoming Range and 
the western Wind River Range if banding sets up right. The only 
location with a greater than 1 in 2 chance of 4 inches or more is 
the highest elevations of the Wind River Range though, so now 
highlights will be issued. A few showers are possible East of the 
Divide, but the chance is generally less than 1 out of 3 and any 
amounts should be rather light.

Wednesday and Thursday look more tranquil as ridging builds 
over the area and brings dry conditions and above normal 
temperatures. The next concern shifts to a potential weekend 
system that could bring the next round of rain and / or snow. 
There has been somewhat in slowing of the progress of the 
system, so Friday may end up being mild and dry as well,
especially East of the Divide. Most of the weekend details are 
still uncertain. The best chance of showers would be across 
western mountains through most of Sunday, but there is a large 
spread in guidance as to how numerous showers would be. However,
Sunday night into Monday are starting to look interesting. A 
closed flow may pass near or just south of Wyoming and with 
north flow into the area, it may be cold enough for the first 
accumulating snow in many of the lower elevations East of the 
Divide. Now, it is still a weak out and a lot can change, but it
is something to watch as we head later in the week and into the
weekend.
